questions.q: What is this course's throughline, across all seven chapters?
options: Taking the object hierarchy, ingestion, and pipeline concepts Azure Databricks & Delta Lake already introduced and going deep on production-scale governance, ingestion, orchestration, performance, and security
Re-teaching clusters, notebooks, and basic Delta Lake entirely from scratch
Replacing the need to ever use Unity Catalog
Teaching a brand-new platform unrelated to anything covered in the Databricks & Delta Lake course
questions.explain: This course explicitly assumed the fundamentals Azure Databricks & Delta Lake already taught, and built production-scale depth on top of that foundation.

questions.q: What did the capstone project (Lesson 33) actually prove, according to this lesson?
options: That this course's own decisions — Unity Catalog structure, ingestion pattern, Lakeflow pipeline, orchestration, performance and security — actually compose into one governed system
That column masks are unnecessary in a real pipeline
That streaming ingestion should always run inside the same Job as batch orchestration
That this course's ideas only apply to retail data and nowhere else
questions.explain: The capstone is proof the earlier chapters' techniques work together on one real lakehouse, not six isolated examples.

questions.q: Does finishing this course complete the entire Databricks/Lakehouse Engineer career path, according to this lesson's verification?
options: Yes — Kafka & Event Streaming, Airflow, Terraform & Bicep, and Data Engineering Career & Capstone were already built, so finishing this course completes both the Job Ready and Advanced stages, all nine courses
No — Kafka & Event Streaming still needs to be built after this course
No — this course has no relationship to the Databricks/Lakehouse Engineer path at all
Yes, but only the Job Ready stage — the Advanced stage still has courses remaining
questions.explain: All four of the other Advanced-stage courses were already complete before this course started, and the Job Ready stage was already complete as well — this course was the last piece.

questions.q: What structure does this lesson suggest for presenting the capstone in an interview?
options: The same project-story structure from Career & Capstone's own guidance — situation, design decisions, trade-offs, what you'd change — applied to Databricks-specific decisions
Reciting the entire Lakeflow pipeline code line by line with no explanation
Only mentioning that the project used Databricks, without any other detail
There is no recommended structure — improvise entirely
questions.explain: Databricks-specific decisions worth naming out loud include why streaming and batch ingestion were orchestrated separately and why the security model was designed into the catalog structure from the start.

questions.q: Why does this lesson have no "Check yourself" question, unlike every other lesson in the course?
options: There's no next lesson in this course or next course in the path's Advanced stage — readiness is instead being able to explain the capstone's own architecture to someone else
This lesson was left unfinished on purpose
Check-yourself questions are only used in Chapter 1
The quiz below replaces the need for any written guide content
questions.explain: Every other lesson's 'Check yourself' question checks readiness for what comes next — the finale has no next lesson or course to prepare for.
